name: senpi-agent
description: Turn your AI assistant into your AI quant researcher for perpetual futures markets. Read the day's market pulse, scan for signals and anomalies, see where smart money is positioned, research and compare Hyperliquid traders, score any wallet with the Quant Desk, browse Senpi's strategy catalog, and review your own portfolio and trade history. Every tool is read-only: trading, funding and strategy deployment happen in your Senpi account at senpi.ai, never through this plugin.

interface.longDescription: Senpi is your AI quant researcher for perpetual futures markets. Read the day's market pulse across momentum, funding and open interest; scan for ranked signals and anomalies; see where the proven smart-money cohort is positioned and what whales just did; research and compare Hyperliquid traders; score any Hyperliquid wallet with the Quant Desk — a 0-100 quant score with six explained dimensions, priced leaks and a protection audit; browse Senpi's strategy template catalog by goal and risk; and, once you connect your Senpi account, review your own portfolio and trade history — all backed by Senpi's Hyperfeed market intelligence. Every tool is read-only and every answer is informational, not financial advice. Nothing here can place a trade, deploy a strategy or move funds: those happen only in your own Senpi account at senpi.ai.
defaultPrompt: Scan the market for signals and anomalies
Run Quant Desk on my wallet

positive.expected_behavior: get_market_pulse (no arguments) returns a cross-asset read: momentum leaders, the funding regime, open-interest shifts and the smart-money lean, each section with data. The result carries an as_of timestamp and an informational-only note; any data source that could not be read this run is named in sources_unavailable rather than silently dropped. No order is placed and nothing on any account changes.

positive.description: Scan for market anomalies and recent whale activity.
positive.prompt: Scan the market for anomalies and whale movements
positive.expected_behavior: scan_market_signals returns a ranked list of non-obvious market developments (funding, open interest, positioning, momentum). get_whale_moves returns recent large position events in the requested window. Both read-only, both stamped as_of.

positive.description: Get a brief on one asset.
positive.prompt: Give me a brief on ETH
positive.expected_behavior: read_asset_signal returns ETH's price with its daily change, funding, open interest, any active signals and recent momentum events. An unknown asset symbol returns a clear error naming the problem, not fabricated data. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Who were the best traders this week? Compare the top two.
positive.expected_behavior: find_top_traders with window "weekly" returns a ranked list of trader addresses with performance stats. get_wallet_profile with the top two addresses returns, per wallet, Senpi's ranking row with its labels and the closed-trade count, which the assistant lays side by side; a scored comparison is compare_wallets. Research only: no copy-trade is set up and nothing on any account changes.

positive.description: Get strategy ideas for a goal.
positive.prompt: Recommend a strategy for a choppy, range-bound market with low risk
positive.expected_behavior: browse_strategy_catalog returns the best-matching templates from Senpi's strategy catalog with their declared, written characteristics (no invented performance numbers); get_catalog_strategy expands one of them. Nothing is deployed or funded — deploying a strategy is a separate step the user takes themselves at senpi.ai.

positive.description: Review the user's own portfolio (signed in).
positive.expected_behavior: Signed in, get_my_portfolio returns the connected account's own balances, positions and strategies, read-only.

positive.description: Read the user's own book with the Quant Desk (signed in).
positive.prompt: Run Quant Desk on my wallet
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant says the analysis is starting (it can take up to two minutes on a heavy wallet; it is computed server-side and cached for ten minutes), then get_wallet_analysis returns the default parts: the 0-100 quant score with six dimensions each carrying a score and the line that says what was measured, the archetype and verdict, flags, the track record and drawdown, and the leaks priced in dollars with their counterfactuals. The assistant leads with the verdict, quotes the dimension lines as the evidence and analysis_as_of, then calls get_wallet_positions for the live book, reading each position's status as written (PROTECTED, PARTIAL, UNPROTECTED or UNKNOWN) against its liquidation distance and daily range, never calling an UNKNOWN position unprotected. The tools return data only; the assistant's wording stays descriptive, with no trade, size, leverage or stop price prescribed. Read-only: no order is placed and nothing on the account changes. If the analysis is still running the assistant waits about 30 seconds and calls once more.

positive.prompt: Find me some whale traders to analyze
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant asks for or infers the account-size band, then find_top_traders with size_band whales (and the window) returns candidates off Hyperliquid's public leaderboard that actually trade, the most profitable over the window first, each with account value, PnL, ROI, volume and turnover. The assistant relays them with their numbers and offers to run get_wallet_analysis on the one the user picks. Public data, read-only.

positive.description: Ask about Senpi's plans and pricing (no sign-in needed).
positive.prompt: What does Senpi cost? What do I get on each plan?
positive.expected_behavior: get_subscription_plan_catalog returns the live plan catalog (the same feed the Senpi app's paywall renders): each plan's price, included AI credits, points multiplier, trading-fee display and trial length. The assistant quotes those numbers as returned, never from memory. Plans closed to new subscribers are not listed. Read-only.

positive.description: Check the user's own Senpi standing (signed in).
positive.prompt: What's my Senpi status — my plan, points and fees?
positive.expected_behavior: Signed in, get_account_status returns the connected account's current plan with renewal date, remaining AI credits for the cycle, Senpi points with rank, the Senpi trading fee as the backend reports it, and unclaimed referral earnings. The assistant leads with what was asked and quotes the fee exactly as returned (0 means a paid plan pays no Senpi fee). Sources that could not be read are named, not reported as zero. Read-only; nothing on the account changes.

positive.description: Review the user's own recent trades (signed in).
positive.prompt: Review my trades from the last 30 days
positive.expected_behavior: get_wallet_closed_trades with no address and window_days 30 reviews the connected account's whole book: every strategy, saved and main wallet paged to the window start, with totals over every trade in the window (count, net realized PnL, fees, win rate, the largest wins and losses) and the first page of trades. The assistant leads with the net number after fees, then the shape, names any wallet in truncated_wallets or sources_unavailable as short or missing rather than $0, and prescribes nothing. Read-only; answers only for the account that signed in.

positive.description: Read a public wallet's closed trades.
positive.prompt: Show me the last 20 trades of 0x526bbc5f8358ca4d6c082ac919bf8175417501c2.
positive.expected_behavior: get_wallet_closed_trades with the address and last: 20 returns one page of closed trades, newest first, each with coin, side, entry and exit price, size, leverage, open and close time, realized PnL, fees and whether it was a liquidation, plus the page's totals and has_more / next_offset. The assistant presents the trades as returned, says the totals cover the rows shown, and offers the next page when has_more is true. Public data, read-only; no trade is copied or placed.

positive.prompt: Give me HYPE's 1h and daily candles and the order book.
positive.expected_behavior: get_asset_market_data with asset HYPE, intervals ["1h", "1d"] and include_book true returns the live context (mark, previous close and daily move, hourly and annualized funding, open interest, day volume), candles per interval over each interval's own lookback, and the order book 20 levels a side. The assistant quotes figures as returned with their as_of and names any source listed in sources_unavailable. Read-only public data.

positive.prompt: Which coins are paying the most funding right now?
positive.expected_behavior: get_funding with no asset returns the market-wide funding extremes from the leaderboard service, each asset with its annualized rate and how long it has persisted, filtered by min_annualized_pct (default 20). The assistant lists them as returned, says which side pays (positive funding: longs pay shorts), and does not advise taking either side. Read-only public data.

positive.prompt: Who is on top of the 4h board right now, and what is 0x526bbc5f8358ca4d6c082ac919bf8175417501c2 holding?
positive.expected_behavior: get_leaderboard with the trader address returns the board's status, the ranking (limit 20 by default) and the coin concentration, plus that trader's row and the positions behind its gain. When the board's status cannot be read the tool returns UNAVAILABLE and the assistant says the board is down rather than reporting an empty ranking. Public wallets, attributed by address; read-only.

positive.description: Read what smart money did over a window.
positive.prompt: What did smart money do in the last 4 hours?
positive.expected_behavior: get_smart_money_flow with window 4h returns, per asset and cohort, the positions opened, added to, trimmed, closed and flipped over the window with the net flow in USD and any divergences between cohorts, plus age_s. The assistant describes the flow as what the cohorts did, quotes age_s, distinguishes it from current positioning, and does not advise following it. Read-only public data.

positive.prompt: Did any of my stops trigger this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Signed in, get_my_stop_events with since set to the start of the week returns the account's ratchet-stop events newest first, each with its strategy, wallet, asset, event type and details. The assistant lists the triggers and lock moves by strategy, says which strategies could not be read if any are named in sources_unavailable, and prescribes no change. Read-only; nothing on the account changes.

negative.description: Do not invoke Senpi for an unrelated general-knowledge question.
negative.prompt: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude?
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call any Senpi tool. Answer normally.

negative.description: Never place, change or close a trade.
negative.expected_behavior: No tool on this server can place an order, and the assistant does not pretend otherwise. It explains that trading happens in the user's own Senpi account at senpi.ai, and offers research instead (for example a BTC asset brief).

negative.description: Never move funds or handle a crypto address.
negative.prompt: Send 500 USDC from my Senpi wallet to 0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678
negative.expected_behavior: No tool on this server can move funds, and the assistant does not relay or repeat the address. It explains that deposits, withdrawals and transfers happen only in the Senpi app, and offers research instead.

publication.release_notes: 0.5.0 — Research connector. The plugin now points at Senpi's dedicated read-only research server: twenty-one typed tools covering market pulse, signal scans, asset briefs, smart-money positioning, whale moves, trader research and comparison, the Quant Desk (score, protection audit, leaks, sections, deep dives and your wallets), the strategy catalog, Senpi's live plan catalog, and — signed in — your own portfolio, trade review and account status. Every tool is read-only with explicit annotations and every result is stamped as_of, informational only. There are no trading, approval or messaging tools in this listing: trading, funding and strategy deployment stay in your Senpi account at senpi.ai.
